title: Flipside
body: You pitch. They watch. One phone.
notes: I asked it to explain itself, so this is what it made. Flipside is for the pitch that happens in person, across a table or standing next to someone. Their side, my side. Same phone.

title: You moved here to bump into people
body: San Francisco, New York. The whole point is one conversation.
visual: Three small line-drawn scenes in a row: a realtor, a founder and a doctor, each across a table from one person with a phone standing between them.
notes: Everyone in this room moved to a city like this to meet someone. You bump into the right person and you have ninety seconds. Right now that ninety seconds is you holding up your phone, flipping between LinkedIn, a website, a deck, presenting and driving on the same screen. It's distracting, it looks like everyone else, and nobody has built a tool for this.

title: Their screen. Your screen.
body: Direct on one. Present on the other.
visual: The phone standing at 90 degrees, two faces labeled Them and You.
notes: The Duo gives each of you a screen. They get the show. I get the controls: my notes, the next card, a live view of what they're seeing. Nothing gets turned around. The hinge is doing the work, not a button.

title: Say it, and it's a deck
body: Card by card, while you keep talking.
visual: The streaming state: a slide card with the title landed, body lines mid-fade, and a verdigris glow on the border.
notes: You just watched it make this one. Two minutes ago there was no deck about Flipside. It listens the whole time, so if you ask me something mid-pitch it can put the answer on your side while I keep going. Someone give me a topic.

title: Point at things
body: Your finger here. A dot there.
visual: The phone in laptop pose: a trackpad on the flat half, a red dot on the standing half.
notes: Old habit, reaching over and smudging someone's screen. My finger stays on my half and the dot lands on yours. And if you want to point at something, that's for their screen.

title: Close the phone
visual: The phone shut, and a recap notification on a second phone.
notes: Every pitch in this city ends with "I'll send you something." Nobody does. Flipside sends it when I close the phone. That's what a folding phone is for: two people, two sides, one conversation. That's Flipside.
